title: Meta hyperscale data center campus approved by Mason County Fiscal Court (Maysville area, KY)

facts.name: Meta hyperscale data center campus, Mason County (Chrisham LLC, Meta subsidiary)
facts.city: Maysville area (unincorporated Mason County; Maysville is county seat)
facts.latlon_note: Coordinates are for Maysville (county seat), Wikipedia; the campus itself is unincorporated.
facts.investment_note: County Judge-Executive McNeill: initial investment $15 billion. County attorney Parsons: about $10 billion per phase. A reported $800 billion 40-year bond figure was called misleading by Parsons.
facts.jobs_note: 400 is described as a guaranteed minimum of long-term jobs.
facts.power_note: Page describes a 2.2 GW data center in its lead and photo caption; no MW figure in body text.
facts.agreement: Development and community revenue agreement; bonds structured as lease-back; payments in lieu of property taxes to county and school district; about $80M county revenue over five years; roughly $130M for water, roads and public safety; about $45M for a new Maysville water treatment facility; about $5M emergency communications center.
facts.vote: Fiscal Court voted unanimously (tally not in page text per extraction; date Tuesday Oct. 13)

summary: Mason County Fiscal Court approved a development and community revenue agreement for a Meta hyperscale data center campus on about 2,900 acres bought by a Meta subsidiary. A lawsuit against the project has since been reported.
source_title: WVXU — Meta to build data center outside Maysville, Kentucky
verbatim: "a Meta subsidiary known as Chrisham LLC, which is purchasing roughly 2,900 acres of land for the data center." "Initial investment will be $15 billion, 2,000 construction and trades jobs," "guaranteed minimum of 400 high-paying, career making, youth-retaining jobs"
notes: Company named as Meta via its subsidiary Chrisham LLC. Investment figures conflict within the same article ($15B initial vs $10B per phase); both are recorded. Verbatim strings are as returned by the WebFetch extraction of the WVXU page, so re-check them against the live page in the evidence gate. The second source was seen in search results only, not fetched. A lawsuit was reported filed after the vote and is not verified here.

title: AWS 36-building campus, Homer City Energy Campus (Indiana County, PA): county accepts preliminary land development application

facts.name: AWS Homer City Energy Campus (PIT100 Masterplan)
facts.filer: Amazon Web Services (per Indiana Gazette, fetched); Amazon Data Services, Inc. named as filer in search-result summaries only
facts.city: Homer City (campus in Center and Blacklick townships)
facts.latlon_note: Homer City borough centroid (Wikipedia). Campus lies in Center and Blacklick townships, not the borough itself.
facts.acreage_note: Indiana Gazette says about 1,100 acres; a search summary cites about 2,200 acres. Conflict unresolved.
facts.power_note: Campus relies on a 4.5 GW gas generation facility being built by Homer City Redevelopment (search-result summary only, not fetched). No MW figure for AWS load is given in the fetched text.
facts.claimed_jobs_permanent: 1,500-2,000 (search-result summaries of AWS statements; not in fetched text)
facts.incentives: AWS reportedly does not request county or local tax incentives (search-result summary; not in fetched text)

summary: Amazon Web Services filed a preliminary land development plan for a 36-building data center campus at the Homer City Energy Campus. The Indiana County Planning Commission accepted the application for consideration, and the review period runs to January 12, 2027.
source_title: Indiana Gazette — County planners accept for review Amazon's plan for data centers
verbatim: The Indiana County Planning Commission "accepted for consideration a preliminary land development plan application from Amazon Web Services." AWS plans "for 36 data centers together with ancillary office and storage space." The article describes "approximately 1,100 acres of the Homer City Energy Campus," "situated in Center and Blacklick townships."
notes: Event date is the county acceptance (article dated Oct 14, updated Oct 16). A search summary says AWS filed Aug 28 and the planning commission tabled the application Sept 9; those dates were not fetched and are not in the record. The Indiana Gazette text was returned ROT47-encoded by the fetch tool and decoded in extraction, so re-check the live page. The DCD page returned 403 and was not fetched. Power, jobs and incentive facts come from search summaries, not fetched text, and should not ship until confirmed.

title: AWS $6 billion data center investment: King George County Board of Supervisors reaches agreement with AWS

facts.name: AWS King George data center campus (Kings Highway west settlement area; former Birchwood Power Facility property)
facts.latlon_note: County seat coordinates (Wikipedia). Campus is on Route 3 (Kings Highway) west settlement area.
facts.instrument: Mutual agreement between the county and AWS; not a permit. AWS has vested rights to repurpose the former Birchwood Power Facility property; AWS made a binding commitment not to construct data center buildings on land adjacent to the Rappahannock River.

summary: King George County's Board of Supervisors and AWS reached a mutual agreement on AWS's planned $6 billion data center investment on the former Birchwood Power Facility property. The page describes an agreement, not a permit approval.
source_title: County of King George, VA — Agreement Reached on Data Center Campus
verbatim: "reached a mutual agreement regarding AWS's planned $6 billion investment." "is expected to create more than 100 new jobs" "AWS made a binding commitment to not construct data center buildings on land adjacent to the Rappahannock River."
notes: Primary county source; it is the county's own newsflash. The page names AWS, Inc., an Amazon.com company. Power and acreage are not stated. A zoning or permit step may still follow, so the status stays announced.

jurisdiction: Barber County (near Sharon, about 8 miles east of Medicine Lodge)
title: Google 'Project Helium' data center approved by Barber County Commission (Sharon, KS), Google's first Kansas data center

facts.name: Project Helium
facts.latlon_note: Sharon, Kansas (Wikipedia). Wikipedia's lead calls it Kiowa County; the infobox and body say Barber County.
facts.construction_jobs: thousands of temporary construction jobs (no number)
facts.cooling: air-cooled, closed-loop; no new water well on the property (agreement term)
facts.fiscal: Kansas tax exemption up to 20 years for large-scale data centers; estimated county property tax nearly $10M per year; agreement sets daytime and nighttime decibel limits.

summary: The Barber County Commission approved a development agreement for Google's first Kansas data center, Project Helium, near Sharon. Google estimates about 500 permanent jobs and initial operations in 2030.
source_title: KWCH — Barber County Commission approves agreement for Google data center
verbatim: "On Monday morning, in a final vote of 2-0-1, the Barber County Commission approved Google's first Kansas data center in Sharon." "It will be air-cooled and create 500 jobs once finished, as well as thousands of temporary jobs to construct it." "According to Google, the project will be 1.7 million square feet."
notes: The article is dated Aug 30 (a Sunday) but says the vote was 'Monday morning'. Event date is set to Aug 31 from the KWCH URL date; the second URL (a prior-day preview) confirms a pending meeting. The source gives no investment dollar figure or MW. Google's name comes from the article text.

jurisdiction: Milam County (Rockdale, former Alcoa site, about 60 miles NE of Austin)
title: Riot Platforms Rockdale campus: 191 MW, 20-year, $9.1B data center lease reported as Anthropic (Milam County, TX)

facts.name: Riot Platforms Rockdale campus (build-to-suit Tier 3 data center)
facts.tenant_status: Unconfirmed. Riot named the tenant only as 'one of the world's leading frontier AI labs.' Bloomberg, citing sources close to the deal, reported Anthropic is the tenant. Neither company confirmed on the record.
facts.power_note: 191 MW of critical IT capacity (IT load, not gross).
facts.investment_note: Initial 20-year contract revenue about $9.1B; about $16.1B if both five-year extensions are exercised.
facts.delivery: initial 96 IT MW expected December 2027; full 191 IT MW by June 2028
facts.acreage_note: Riot bought the 200-acre Rockdale site in January 2026 (search summary, not fetched).

summary: Riot Platforms disclosed a 191 MW, 20-year data center lease at its Rockdale campus, worth about $9.1 billion, with the tenant described only as a frontier AI lab. Bloomberg reported the tenant is Anthropic, but neither company confirmed it.
source_title: Riot Platforms — Q2 2026 results exhibit (EX-99.1), Rockdale data center lease
verbatim: "with one of the world's leading frontier AI labs, for 191 MW of critical IT capacity at Riot's Rockdale campus." "The Data Center Lease carries an initial term of 20 years, running through June 2048," "with the initial 96 IT MW expected in December 2027 and full 191 IT MW deployment expected by June 2028"
notes: Lease facts are from Riot's SEC exhibit (primary). The Anthropic identification rests on Bloomberg sourcing and must not be presented as company-confirmed. Verbatim for the attribution from the Yahoo/Bloomberg article: 'Bloomberg cited sources close to the deal who confirmed the Claude creator is behind the deal.' and 'Neither company responded to requests for comment.' Decide whether an unconfirmed tenant should ship under an anthropic company slug or be filed as a Riot project with the tenant noted in offtaker. Dated Aug 10 disclosure, Bloomberg attribution Aug 12.

summary: The City of Blakely approved a memorandum of understanding with Early County and QTS on the Project Blue Hole data center, with QTS paying $7.5M for the first phase and $7M a year after.
source_title: WTVY — Blakely approves agreement with QTS Data Centers related to proposed facility
